traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements for Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING are satisfied.
• Core functionality & specificity (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC): Each validation rule defines focused, descriptive meta.messages entries using ESLint’s messageId mechanism. Dedicated tests in tests/rules/*.test.ts verify specific messages for missing annotations, invalid formats, missing files, and missing requirement IDs.
• Location & context (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT): Messages use placeholders like {{name}}, {{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{path}}, {{reqId}}, and {{storyPath}}, and rule implementations report on the appropriate AST node so ESLint surfaces precise locations. The error-reporting test explicitly asserts correct data payload ({ name: 'bar', functionName: 'bar' }).
• Suggestions (REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION): require-story-annotation sets hasSuggestions: true and the error-reporting.test.ts suite confirms that suggestions are produced with a concrete, example-based description and a fix function, giving clear, actionable remediation steps.
• Consistency across rules (REQ-ERROR-CONSISTENCY): Message templates align with the conventions described in the story: function errors mention the function name; branch errors use "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}."; format errors share "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}."; file and requirement reference errors consistently include the relevant path/ID placeholders.
• Error handling (edge cases): valid-story-reference differentiates missing files from filesystem errors (fileMissing vs fileAccessError) and enforces project boundaries; valid-annotation-format reports configuration errors via invalidRuleConfiguration without aborting validation, satisfying robustness expectations.
• Severity configuration (REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY): src/index.ts encodes the error vs warning mapping, and tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts includes [REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY] checks, confirming that ESLint configs apply the intended severities.
All related tests, including the dedicated error-reporting suite and config/structure tests, pass in the latest Jest run. No contradictions with the story were found, so the story is fully implemented and verified.
